Provides: Transparency • Look at the underlying code of models Flexibility • Can tweak models to represent a new or unusual configuration Standards • Provides standards for all models, including closed-source Collaboration • New technology models that might not yet have a commercial market • Encourages collaboration amongst taxpayer funded projects NREL | 8 Licensing Entity 2017-2019 License Current License MIT-type license with no BSD3-clause (no sharing Commercial Entities sharing restrictions restrictions) BSD3-clause (no sharing Research and Non-profit GPLv3 like license with restrictions) Entities sharing required Lesson learned: standard licenses make it easier for contributors NREL | 9 Open-Source Contributors • Other NREL teams • Sandia National Laboratories • Cypress Creek Renewables • Envision Digital • OpenInvest • Passivenous Consulting • Southern Company NREL | 10 Types of Contributions Report bugs Publish NREL Adding directly to Fix compiler battery additional PV GitHub with warnings degradation sub-models line numbers models Write no code Write large modules NREL | 11 Large Successful Contributions • Mermoud/Lejeune module model - Included unit tests, released as an SDK option - Received subsequent open-source contributions with extensions and fixes • Slope-aware backtracking algorithm - Able to keep the original author aware of updates • Chemistry specific battery degradation algorithms NREL | 12 Reasons to Contribute • Prestige – Contributions are public • Solving business needs • Unofficial “stamp of approval” – Able to say changes are in the official NREL SAM repository NREL | 13 Challenges • Language choice - C++ is fast, but smaller pool of developers • Desktop GUI increases user base, but adds another barrier to contributions - Core team
